title: Raw adic finite classical strata transport
statement: Fix D, prime l different from D.p, an algebraic closure Omega, and the comparison interfaces [def-zl-raw-heart-adic-lisse-data]. Let a, c, b, S, r be supplied families with HeartComparison on each geometric base. Fix a separated finite-type geometric base X, a finite coefficient stage i, a finite sf heart object N at i, a continuous rational module F with an explicit finite locally closed lisse-partition witness, and an isomorphism from the r-realization of S(N) to F[0]. There is a finite reduced locally closed partition of X with separated finite-type geometric bases and their correct structure maps, and on each stratum a classical finite-free raw rational system at the same stage i whose b-realization is isomorphic to the actual finite derived restriction of N. The statement chooses neither a common-stage representative nor a Weil structure nor a frontier.

source.place: Section 6.8, Lemma 6.8.2, Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4), Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; blueprint latest thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves proof paragraphs 6-7, agent interface transport.

proof.text: Use the supplied finite-stage heart object N and its specified continuous constructible realization F in degree zero. Apply the stratified-lattice theorem to its finite lisse-partition witness. It gives a finite reduced refinement and lisse integral lattices whose localizations are the restrictions of F, all at E. Give each stratum the structure map induced from X; an immersion into a separated finite-type scheme over a field is separated finite type. These are the bases and the base_map equations. The completed-system comparison takes each lattice to its ordinary finite-free etale quotient tower. Regard that tower as the object of RawRational with the canonical ULift coefficient identification. The normalized continuous pullback comparison carries N restricted to the stratum to F there. The specified lattice-localization isomorphism and the comparison for b identify the two continuous derived images. Lift this isomorphism through the fully faithful continuous realization and the identity sf/PBC equivalence, orienting it from the raw restriction to the classical realization. This is the restriction field of the conclusion. No common-stage representative is selected here. On the empty scheme the partition is empty, and zero local ranks use zero towers; no extension of E or assertion about derived reductions of a torsion representative is needed.
